Neginoth
neg-ee-NOHTH
noun
Hebrew neginōth, plural of negināh, from nāgan, “to touch the strings, to play a stringed instrument”; music made upon strings, as harp, psaltery, and lyre.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Neginoth is the direction “to the chief Musician on Neginoth,” standing over several psalms (4, 6, 54, 55, 67, 76) and answered in Habakkuk’s closing word, “to the chief singer on my stringed instruments” (Hab 3:19). It appoints the psalm to be sung with the accompaniment of strings. The worship of Israel was no formless thing left to the whim of the worshipper; David, by the word of the LORD through Gad and Nathan, set the Levites in their courses “to be the singers with instruments of musick, psalteries and harps and cymbals” (1Ch 15:16; 2Ch 29:25). Neginoth witnesses to that ordered, appointed praise. The strings were no mere ornament but the servants of the word, lifting the holy text upon a fitting tune that the congregation might sing it together with one heart and voice. Let the believer learn the principle that abides through every age: God is to be worshipped not as men devise, but as He appoints; with reverence and order, “decently and in order” (1Co 14:40), the affections engaged and the body bowed, the whole man and the whole assembly brought under the rule of His revealed will. The form serves the word, and the word serves the glory of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Stringed instruments, or music upon strings; the direction appointing a psalm to be sung with such accompaniment.

expand to see more

NEGINOTH, a Hebrew word in the titles of several psalms, signifying stringed instruments.

It is derived from a root meaning to touch the strings or to play upon them.

The direction “to the chief Musician on Neginoth” appoints the psalm to be sung with strings.

It witnesses to the ordered, appointed worship David set among the Levites.

It teaches that the form of worship is the servant of the word and the glory of God.

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 4, title — "To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David."

Hab 3:19 — "The LORD God is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds’ feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places. To the chief singer on my stringed instruments."

1Ch 15:16 — "And David spake to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brethren to be the singers with instruments of musick, psalteries and harps and cymbals, sounding, by lifting up the voice with joy."

1Co 14:40 — "Let all things be done decently and in order."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A direction for ordered praise; it rebukes the modern drift from reverent, appointed worship toward performance staged for the worshipper’s entertainment.

expand to see more

Neginoth itself faces no postmodern redefinition, but the worship it served is everywhere under pressure. The age tends to treat the gathering of the saints as a concert — a stage, a spectacle, a performance measured by its power to move and to please the crowd — rather than as the appointed, reverent, congregational praise of a holy God who has told us how He will be worshipped.

The principle to recover is order under the word. The strings of Neginoth were appointed servants of the holy text, set in their place by David at God’s direction, that the whole congregation might sing as one. Worship is not ours to devise after the fashion of the world; it is to be rendered “decently and in order,” the form forever bowing to the word it carries and to the glory of the God it adores.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for playing upon strings, Neginoth appoints a psalm to ordered, instrument-bearing congregational praise.

expand to see more

Neginoth — Hebrew neginōth, from nāgan, to play upon strings.

The direction “to the chief Musician on Neginoth” heads psalms 4, 6, 54, 55, 67, and 76.

Habakkuk closes “to the chief singer on my stringed instruments.”

David appointed the Levites with psalteries, harps, and cymbals (1Ch 15:16).

It witnesses to ordered worship, the form serving the word.

Usage

"Neginoth marks the appointed, reverent praise of Israel, the strings made servants of the holy word."

"God is worshipped not as men devise but as He appoints, decently and in order."

"The form of worship forever bows to the word it carries and the glory of the God it adores."
